A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Local MDI+ research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and real-data experiments on feature identification, stability, ablations, counterfactuals, and subgroup discovery, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional ensemble-configuration, full-dataset, and runtime results.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 retains the expanded node/raw-feature representation, regularized GLM, coefficient-product attributions, zero scores for unused features, and averaging across trees. Gradient boosting is newly evaluated without a distinct attribution procedure. The stump-formula correction aligns the equation with the node-supported construction already described in v1.

E1.justification: The twelve real datasets and principal evaluation tasks remain unchanged. However, Section 4.1 replaces the pure interaction response with an additive-plus-polynomial-interaction response, revising the synthetic signal structure being recovered. Larger samples and additional ensemble configurations do not themselves introduce new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 5 adds Local MDI to the subgroup comparison, previously containing LIME, TreeSHAP, and global OLS. Table 2 also includes Local MDI when ranking each ablated variant, whereas v1 compares each variant against LIME and TreeSHAP. These are comparator-membership changes independent of the LMDI/Local MDI naming changes elsewhere.

E3.justification: Semi-synthetic sample sizes change from {150, 500, 1000} to {300, 500, 1000}, and the Linear+LSS response expands from three terms to five. v2 adds full-dataset evaluations reaching 72,000 observations, alternative RF and boosting configurations, and runtime experiments varying leaf size and ensemble size. Section 5 also revises its stated sample sizes and retention range to match settings already plotted in v1's stability appendix; this correction alone does not establish a changed experiment.

E4.justification: Section 6 and new Appendix F extend component ablations with sensitivity to forest size, minimum leaf size, and gradient boosting. Section 9 adds runtime-scaling analyses, while Appendix D.3 tests whether feature-selection findings persist beyond downsampling. These substantially extend the original component, correlation, and application analyses.

E5.justification: The corresponding experiments retain 30 synthetic runs, 50 correlation runs, 20 real-data runs, and 15 stability runs, with standard-error reporting. Stability still compares five RF fits with different seeds. The new result tables introduce no stated new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Benchmark curves, ablation ranks, and counterfactual values are revised. For example, LMDI+'s House 16H counterfactual distance changes from 7.8 to 7.6, while Higgs changes from 18.1 to 18.2 in v1 Table 3 versus v2 Table 4. New ensemble, full-dataset, and runtime results substantially expand the evidence. Revised synthetic results use changed response functions or sample sizes and do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 3 replaces threshold-only indicators with explicit membership in the left and right child nodes. This corrects the displayed stump function so it is zero outside the split node. Proposition 1 and Appendix A's mathematical formulation remain substantively unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central signal-identification, stability, and application claims remain, including the abstract's average 10% improvement claim. v2 newly foregrounds gains extending to gradient boosting and the contribution of individual components. v1 discussed application beyond random forests primarily as a future extension.

C2.justification: v2 refines explanations of overfitting and correlated-feature bias, and distinguishes costly model refitting from efficient inference with fixed GLM coefficients. Its limitations now acknowledge incomplete ensemble-configuration coverage. Figure 7's interpretation is also qualified from general superiority to competitiveness, emphasizing advantages at low PVE.

D1.justification: v2 adds the 16-CPU-core runtime configuration and discussion of parallel computation across trees. Most RF and GLM settings move from v1 Appendix B into Section 4, but the previously stated logistic solver='saga' detail is omitted. Both PDFs retain links to the same implementation and experimental repositories.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands substantially through the PCS framework, explicit treatment of Sutera et al.'s Local MDI, MAPLE, permutation-based global importance, and additional attribution-evaluation and stability literature. These additions change how the contribution is situated relative to existing methods and methodological principles, beyond the switch to author-year citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and contribution list, MDI-bias explanations, local-attribution motivation, and discussion receive broad rewriting and expansion. Implementation details move into the main experimental section, runtime analysis becomes a separate section, and the appendices are reorganized to accommodate full-dataset results and ensemble ablations.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different journal layout with revised typography, margins, headers, and author presentation. Table 2 becomes a component checklist, five additional tables display ensemble, runtime, and full-dataset results, and multiple plots receive revised axes, legends, or comparator curves. Existing appendix maps and application illustrations are retained rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked quantitative runtime comparisons and experimental validation beyond its default RF configuration and capped real-data evaluations. v2's ensemble checks, full-dataset evaluations, and timing studies substantially strengthen evidence for practical applicability while revealing computational tradeoffs with TreeSHAP and LIME. The corrected stump equation and fuller treatment of relevant prior work further improve rigor. These gains outweigh the limited reproducibility loss from omitting the previously specified logistic solver.
